segments.title: Chương 310: 0312
segments.content:
Cannes, Palais des Festivals et des Congrès.

The very place where the awards for the Cannes Film Festival are presented.

The venue for the IMGA changed every year. The first was held in Barcelona. This year, it had become increasingly influential, enough to afford renting the Palais des Festivals.

Just like the film festival, the IMGA also had a slew of exhibition booths.

In the days leading up to the awards ceremony, mobile phone manufacturers and mobile game developers were already creating a buzz in the exhibition area.

This year's naming rights were secured by Nokia, and their logo was visible everywhere. Nokia's booth was particularly massive, with a dazzling array of various phone models on display, where attendees could use Nokia phones to try out all kinds of mobile games.

In the mobile game exhibition area, Gameloft's booth was the largest.

This company was a subsidiary of Ubisoft, had been publicly listed since 1999, and had revenues of nearly a hundred million US dollars last year. This year, they had also brought the famous IP "Prince of Persia" to mobile phones for the first time.

Dingguo Technology's booth was smaller. Of the company's seven-person team, only Tang Kai and Zhang Lei had come; the others had stayed behind in China.

Well, it's not clear what year Xia Siyuan joined Dingguo, but he claimed to have participated in the development of "7 Days" and "Road to the Netherworld"—though the timeline didn't quite add up.

Who is Xia Siyuan, you ask?

The producer of "The Last Ming: Feather of the Void Abyss"... so cringe.

Xia Siyuan left Dingguo Technology in 2015, by which time Dingguo had already been dissolved and reorganized two or three times. Apart from the founder still being Tang Kai, the rest had little to do with "7 Days." He was probably just trying to build up his own reputation.

"Oh! Putain, c'est génial!" a French gamer exclaimed, both praising and cursing while playing "7 Days."

What he said was a French curse word, which could be roughly translated to "Fuck, this is so damn good."

Tang Kai asked Shen Weilun in a low voice, "Brother Shen, not many people here speak English. Do you understand French?"

Shen Weilun was an employee sent by Game Science. He used to be in charge of publicity and marketing at E-Tang's Jinling branch. He was recruited by Qu Guohao and was one of the core members of the Game Science Jinling faction.

"I don't, but judging by their expressions, they seem to be having a great time," Shen Weilun said. "I've already communicated with the competition's organizing committee and have also made preliminary contact with other game developers about agency matters. From their reactions, it's very likely '7 Days' will win an award."

Tang Kai asked curiously, "Can the company influence the award presentation?"

Shen Weilun said, "It's the market that can influence the award presentation. Of course, the premise is that '7 Days' has to be of high quality. Otherwise, we wouldn't even have a chance to pull any strings."

Tang Kai fell silent. He felt that winning an award this way wasn't pure.

Shen Weilun said, "'7 Days' might even get a special award if it doesn't win Best 3D Game. A special award created specifically for the Chinese market!"

"As long as we can win an award, it's good," Tang Kai consoled himself.

The days passed one by one, and the awards ceremony officially began.

At the guest sign-in area by the red carpet entrance was a huge Nokia billboard.

Compared to the Cannes Film Festival, the IMGA still seemed far too quiet. The number of reporters was less than a tenth of that at the film festival.

Tang Kai, Zhang Lei, Shen Weilun, and the others, dressed in suits and ties, walked down the red carpet, smiling and waving at the press photographers on both sides.

"Xiao Tang, look over here!" a Chinese reporter suddenly shouted.

Tang Kai was taken aback.

Shen Weilun explained, "A reporter from 'China Computerworld,' sent on the orders of a leader from the Ministry of Information Industry. This time, '7 Days' wasn't approved by the GAPP, it was only filed with China Mobile and China Unicom for release. Understand?"

Tang Kai didn't understand politics and was a little confused.

Mobile games actually fell under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Information Industry!

In the past, due to the lack of significant mobile game products, the MII itself couldn't be bothered to pay much attention. Now, hearing that a game might win an award, the MII immediately dispatched a reporter from one of its subordinate publications to cover it.

The reason Chen Guiliang had first submitted "7 Days" to the GAPP for approval wasn't to get some license. It was to show his attitude to Director Kou, that he wouldn't easily switch allegiances.

Director Kou personally instructed them to expedite the approval process to show the importance he placed on Game Science. The fact that it ultimately didn't pass was because he didn't want to step on the MII's toes—even though the MII didn't regulate directly, but rather delegated the review authority to China Mobile and China Unicom.

Shen Weilun said, "Whether you win an award or not, you'll need to give an exclusive interview to 'China Computerworld' afterward."

"Alright, I promise to cooperate," Tang Kai said, delighted.

As they spoke, the group had already entered the awards hall.

The awards ceremony officially began, starting with speeches from the leaders.

A local French official spoke, generally about how Cannes was honored to host this year's IMGA, that he personally enjoyed playing mobile games, and that he would pay more attention to the IMGA and mobile games in the future.

Next was a speech from the IMGA chairman, who talked about the development of the global mobile game industry,

and mentioned that the global market size had grown by 47% last year.

The first award announced was the "Technician's Choice Award."

As the name suggested, the judges for this award were all industry technicians.

It was awarded to "Metal Gear Solid Mobile."

The "People's Choice Award" was decided by player votes and was given to "WRC 3D."

Then there was the "Best Licensed IP Game," which went to "Phoebe's Island Adventure."

The "Best 3D Game" award, for which "7 Days" was nominated, was one of the highlights of the evening.

The presenters were two French celebrities, a man and a woman. They gave detailed introductions of the five nominated games and then chatted and joked on stage to liven up the atmosphere.

Finally, the male celebrity said, "And the award for Best 3D Game goes to..."

The female presenter opened the envelope: "From China's Dingguo Technology, '7 Days'!"

The representative from the Korean company PatiGames had a look of disbelief on his face, and immediately started searching for the Korean judge.

They couldn't understand why, with a Korean on the judging panel and a Korean game nominated, the award was ultimately given to a Chinese game.

Amid a round of applause, Tang Kai walked onto the stage.

His English was much more fluent than Chen Guiliang's: "Thank you, IMGA. Thank you, judges. Thank you to all the players... When I quit my job last year to start my own company, I could never have imagined that I would be standing here so soon. Our team has seven people. At the beginning, everyone's monthly salary was 2,000 RMB. Regardless of position, everyone got the same pay..."

"Later, we couldn't even afford the 2,000 RMB monthly salary, and everyone worked for free for the sake of their dream. We even ate instant noodles for a week straight... Just as our funds were about to run out, we were incredibly fortunate to receive an investment from Mr. Chen Guiliang. Mr. Chen made '7 Days' more perfect; otherwise, we wouldn't have had the resources to fix the bugs later on..."

Tang Kai was quite a good storyteller, drawing several rounds of applause from the audience.

The reporter from "China Computerworld" was also hearing this story for the first time and was incredibly moved by it.

Beyond being moved, he was also filled with emotion.

Because Tang Kai hadn't just sought help from one company, nor had he emailed just one company boss. But in the end, the only one who responded was Chen Guiliang.

The awards ceremony continued.

The ultimate award was called the "Grand Prix."

The winning game was "Metal Gear Solid Mobile."

Although this game was a Japanese IP, the mobile version's development had been handed over by Konami to France's Gameloft. This was essentially giving the final grand prize to the host country.

Of course, the publishing rights were still in Konami's hands.

One of the tasks Game Science had sent Shen Weilun to Cannes for was to negotiate the Chinese agency rights for the award-winning works.

He had to drive the price down, otherwise it would be difficult to recoup the cost, and pirated copies would be everywhere before long.

After the awards ceremony, there was a cocktail party.

The reporter from "China Computerworld" had a couple of drinks and then went back to his hotel to file his story to China via email.
